name: Zapier
summary: No-code automation platform that connects apps so a trigger in one starts actions in others, with a free plan and paid tiers by task volume.
best_for: Small teams and founders who want to connect the apps they already use so data moves on its own, and are happy to pay per task as volume grows
skip_if: you only need a single two-step handoff, you want fixed costs that do not grow with usage, you need to self-host your data, or you want a tool we have tested ourselves
honest_knock: Pricing is based on tasks, so a busy month can cost more than the starting price suggests. Free allows only two-step Zaps. Since 15 June 2026 AI steps are priced by model tier and can use more tasks per run.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Professional · Free $0 with 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-16 on zapier.com/pricing, US dollars a month) Zapier connects apps with automations called Zaps. Free costs $0 and includes unlimited Zaps, Tables and Forms, two-step Zaps and 100 tasks a month. Professional starts from $19.99 a month and Team from $69 a month, with 1 seat on Professional and 25 on Team. The page has a Pay yearly toggle that saves 33%, and its text does not say which billing period the starting prices assume. A new account gets a 14-day trial of Professional with no card. You can cancel at any time and keep the plan until the billing cycle ends. A task is any successful action. We have not paid for a plan.

schema_offer.description: Professional, Free $0 with 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps; Professional starting from $19.99 a month; Team starting from $69 a month; yearly toggle saves 33%; billing basis of starting prices unlabeled; 14-day Professional trial, no card. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-16.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Zapier under the automatic 14 day Professional trial, which needs no card: a form feeding a table through a Zap went live a little over 5 minutes after the start, ran 5 times without a failure and used 0 tasks, but the table records stayed empty because the whole submission was mapped to one column, and the Copilot only titled the form without adding its fields. Because everything ran under the trial, what Free allows after it was not tested. The plan page shows euros: Professional €18,62 a month billed annually or €27,93 billed monthly; the public page in US dollars gives $19.99 and $29.99, so the $19.99 in our dossier is the yearly price. The checkout was opened and nothing was paid. Account and start: the account was created by us, who was signed in; our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab of our Chrome, starting at 14:07. The interface was already on English. The profile page said that the current account address needed to be confirmed; the account worked anyway. Onboarding: the role Business Owner (the list had no Founder or Owner), the team size 1-49 (the smallest option; Just me does not exist) and Skip question for the apps. Right after that the home page said 14 TRIAL DAYS LEFT, Plan tasks 0 / 1.000 and Zapier Pro trial ends Dec 2: an automatic Professional trial of 14 days started without a card, while the plan page still calls the account Current plan: Free. Everything that was built therefore ran under the trial and does not prove what Free allows. The dossier name is Zapier and the review is on OSM (zapier-review). The pain that was tested: telling one app when something happens in another, without paying for it. No external app was connected, only the built-in apps Forms and Tables. Core action: a form was built with Home, Form, Blank form. The Copilot said Done! Your form is now titled Test Handoff with three required fields but only set the title; the fields name, email and type had to be added by hand (Add field, a label, Insert field), about 12 clicks and a few failed tries, because the label was only kept after Insert field. The Zap: Automate form, Build your own automation opened a new browser tab with the Zap editor: step 1 Zapier Forms, Form Submission Created, step 2 Zapier Tables, Create Record. Create Table inside the step made a table with a generic name and one column Text Field, so the columns name, email and type do not exist; Form Submission Values was mapped to Text Field. The trigger test found a sample Form Submission A; the test of the Tables step was skipped. Publish said Success! Your Zap is live! (version v1). Time: the Zap went live at 14:12:16 and the first run was at 14:12:29, a little over 5 minutes after the start at 14:07, including the onboarding, the form and the Zap. Five test submissions were sent through the public form page (made up names Test Lead 1 to 5, made up addresses on example.com, type trial), each answered Form submitted!. Zap history showed 5 runs, all Successful, between 14:12:29 and 14:12:49. The run details said Found 1 new Form Submission in Zapier Forms and Sent 1 new Record to Zapier Tables, but the record in the data out had only empty f1 and f2: the column Text Field stayed empty because the whole Form Submission Values block was mapped to one column. So the handoff ran and the data did not arrive in the table. Whether separate fields work with extra columns was not tried. Tasks: Zap history showed a dash for the tasks of each run, Plan tasks stayed 0 / 1.000 after 5 runs, also on Billing & usage, and the tab Task usage said No results found. That is 0 tasks a run for Forms plus Tables; the built-in apps do not seem to count as a task, which is our reading of the counter and was not checked in the help text. Nothing in this Zap needed a paid plan. The plan page lists Multi-step Zaps, Unlimited Premium apps, Webhooks, AI fields and Conditional form logic under Professional. Webhooks by Zapier (Catch Hook) was not tested because Forms worked. The form page showed Free next to the Forms name with View plans and Upgrade, but Forms worked under the trial without a prompt. A second tab of the Zap editor gave a warning about overriding current edits (UpdateBlocked). Plans: The plans were read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 on the plan page in the app (euros, because the app detected the Netherlands) and the public page zapier.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day with the currency set to USD. In euros: Free €0 with 100 tasks /mo; Professional €18,62 /mo billed annually (€27,93 struck through) or €27,93 /mo billed monthly at 750 tasks /mo; Team €64,26 billed annually or €96,40 billed monthly at 2,000 tasks /mo and 25 users; Enterprise on request; Save 33% for annual billing. In US dollars on the public page: Professional $19.99 a month with yearly billing and $29.99 with monthly billing, Team $69 with yearly billing and $103.50 with monthly billing. So the $19.99 in the dossier is the yearly price; the page does not say which billing period the starting price assumes unless the switch is used. Free lists unlimited Zaps, Tables and Forms, two-step Zaps and Copilot with a daily limit; Professional adds multi-step Zaps, unlimited premium apps, webhooks, AI fields and conditional form logic. Checkout: on the plan page Checkout was opened for Professional with 750 tasks. Monthly: Total due today €27,93 and Next monthly charge on december 18, 2026 €27,93 /mo. Annual: Total due today €223,41 and Next annual charge on november 18, 2027; Save 33% and Save €111,76 per year with annual billing. Pay-per-task billing: if it is enabled and the included tasks are exceeded, the checkout says €0,0931 per additional task plus applicable taxes on monthly billing and €0,0311 on annual billing; it can be switched off, and then the Zaps are paused. The checkout showed no separate tax amount: Total due today equalled the plan sum, and plus applicable taxes is only named at the pay-per-task line; the tax probably appears after an address and tax number are added, which was not done. The payment screen offered Card (number, date, CVC, Full name, Country or region Netherlands, Address) and Paypal. Nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. The line Please add a payment method to edit your trial settings. shows that the trial settings need a payment method, although the trial itself started without one. Cancelling: a paid plan can be left through Settings, Billing & usage, Compare plans or Upgrade; this was not tested because there was no paid plan. The trial ends by itself on 2 Dec 2026 without a card. Deleting the account is Settings, Security and data, Delete my account (and Delete my data, which keeps the account); neither was clicked. Not tested: a Zap of more than two steps, Webhooks by Zapier, premium apps, AI steps and their task price, what Free allows after the trial (100 tasks, two-step Zaps), a connection with an outside app, the payment, the tax rule, and cancelling or downgrading a paid plan. Clean up: the Zap is switched OFF (version v1 stays published); the form Test Handoff stays reachable on its public page, the generated table with 5 empty records, the Zap with its 5 runs and the Professional trial until 2 Dec 2026 stay; no card, no payment, no outside apps. Two tabs that the Zapier editor opened by itself fell outside our tab group and could not be closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The plan page calls the account Free while the trial gives the paid features, so a first Zap proves little about the Free plan. The Copilot only titled the form and left the fields to you, and the table that the Zap creates has one generic column, so map the fields one by one. The starting prices depend on yearly billing: monthly billing costs a third more. Pay-per-task billing can charge for tasks above the included number unless you switch it off, and then the Zaps pause. Editing the trial settings needs a payment method.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Zaps of more than two steps, Webhooks by Zapier, premium apps and AI steps with their task price.
What Free allows after the trial (100 tasks, two-step Zaps), because everything ran under the Professional trial.
A connection with an outside app.
Whether separate form fields can fill separate table columns.
Paying, the tax on the checkout and cancelling or downgrading a paid plan.
Deleting the account or the data, which were looked up but not clicked.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 14:07 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
